questions.question: Linux virtual machines must mount an Azure file share by using NFS 4.1. Which storage account should you create for the share?

options.why: Correct. NFS shares are supported only on premium file shares.
Standard accounts support SMB file shares only.
Block blob accounts do not host file shares.

options.text: A standard account with a hierarchical namespace
options.why: Hierarchical namespace accounts support NFS 3.0 for blobs, not NFS file shares.

questions.explanation: NFS 4.1 Azure file shares require a premium FileStorage account and network access through a virtual network.

questions.question: A user deleted a folder from an Azure file share yesterday. The share has share soft delete enabled and daily share snapshots. How should you recover the folder?

options.text: Restore the folder from yesterday's share snapshot
options.why: Correct. Snapshots hold point-in-time copies of files and folders in the share.
Share soft delete restores a deleted share, not a folder in a live share.
This command restores soft-deleted blobs, not files.
Failover changes the primary region and does not recover deleted data.

questions.explanation: Share snapshots recover files and folders. Share soft delete recovers whole shares.

questions.question: What is the maximum number of share snapshots that one Azure file share can keep?

options.why: Correct. Azure Files supports up to 200 snapshots per share.
This is lower than the limit.
This is lower than the limit.
The number of snapshots per share is limited.

questions.explanation: Azure Backup can manage snapshot schedules and retention within this limit.

questions.question: A file share was deleted. Share soft delete is enabled with a retention period of 14 days. The share had three snapshots. What can you restore?

options.text: The share, including its three snapshots
options.why: Correct. Soft-deleted shares are restored together with their snapshots.

options.text: The share, but not its snapshots
options.why: Snapshots are kept with the soft-deleted share.
The whole share is restored.

options.text: Nothing, because shares with snapshots bypass soft delete
options.why: Soft delete covers shares with snapshots.

questions.explanation: Restore the share with az storage share-rm restore or Undelete in the portal during the retention period.

questions.question: You need to create a 2 TiB SMB file share named finance on a standard general-purpose v2 account. The share will have many read and write operations. Which Azure CLI command should you run?

options.text: az storage share-rm create --storage-account stcontoso --name finance --quota 2048 --access-tier TransactionOptimized
options.why: Correct. The quota is in GiB, and the transaction optimized tier suits heavy transaction workloads.

options.text: az storage share-rm create --storage-account stcontoso --name finance --quota 2 --access-tier Premium
options.why: The quota is in GiB, and the Premium tier requires a premium account.

options.text: az storage container create --account-name stcontoso --name finance
options.why: This creates a blob container, not a file share.

options.text: az storage share-rm create --storage-account stcontoso --name finance --enabled-protocols NFS
options.why: NFS is not supported on standard accounts.

questions.explanation: Standard file shares offer the transaction optimized, hot and cool tiers, with quotas up to 100 TiB.
